plainSummary: Agents could still record decisions and approvals after permission ends, including an approval labeled as human.
summary: The shared operation boundary suite ran seven adversarial cases against the current tree: four passed and three failed. Invalid slices are rejected before seal/turn/activation/automation effects; caller-supplied roots are rejected; progress honors permission; and stale revision/source inputs leave domain records unchanged. Decision and code-review writes omit the current permission check, and the portable review operation accepts caller-supplied kind:human/reviewer labels that can satisfy the code-review gate. Receipt killers remain green separately; actual MCP lifecycle coverage is still pending.

findings.gap: packages/ledger/src/application/operations.ts submitDecision checks revision and source but not permissionStatus before writeDecision. The breaker removed all authority from an open workstream turn; executeOperation(record_decision) succeeded instead of returning permission_denied and persisted a decision.
findings.plainImpact: An agent could keep recording consequential decisions after its permission has ended.
findings.fixProposal: Inside the serialized record_decision effect, require current applicable permission for the turn's workstream before calling writeDecision; retain revision/source checks and leave no decision on denial.

evidence.citedTest: packages/ledger/src/application/operations.break.test.ts::denies record_decision without current permission and creates no domain record
evidence.observedOutput: FAIL denies record_decision without current permission and creates no domain record: AssertionError: operation unexpectedly succeeded

findings.gap: packages/ledger/src/application/operations.ts submitReview validates source and open-turn state but not current permission before writeReview and the slice codeBreakReviewId update. The breaker removed all authority; executeOperation(record_review) still saved an approval and updated plan metadata.
findings.plainImpact: A review submitted after permission ends could still clear the code-review checkpoint.
findings.fixProposal: Inside the serialized code-review effect, require current applicable permission for the turn's workstream before writing the review or updating codeBreakReviewId; denial must leave both paths unchanged.

evidence.citedTest: packages/ledger/src/application/operations.break.test.ts::denies record_review without current permission and creates no domain record
evidence.observedOutput: FAIL denies record_review without current permission and creates no domain record: AssertionError: operation unexpectedly succeeded

findings.gap: The portable shared record_review operation accepts review.kind=human and reviewer=human:project-owner from untrusted operation input. writeReview preserves those fields, and isCodeBreakApprove accepts non-discussion human approvals with killersCited, so caller labels can be displayed and evaluated as a human review without host-authenticated provenance. Historical human review records are outside this finding.
findings.plainImpact: An agent could label its own portable review as human-approved and clear the review gate.
findings.fixProposal: Reject kind:human on the portable CLI/MCP review operation and treat reviewer text only as agent-reported attribution; preserve loading of existing historical human records and reserve verified human writes for a bounded host adapter.

evidence.citedTest: packages/ledger/src/application/operations.break.test.ts::does not accept portable review fields that claim human provenance
evidence.observedOutput: FAIL does not accept portable review fields that claim human provenance: AssertionError: operation unexpectedly succeeded

residualRisks: The operation hunt is not complete: actual MCP lifecycle, explicit check execution, completion, and CLI/MCP parity remain for separate run-backed coverage.
Portable reviewer labels remain agent-reported attribution even after kind:human is rejected; stronger reviewer identity requires a host that can attest execution identity.
Receipt concurrency, corrupt replay, unfinished retry, failed completion publication, and unknown-lock killers pass in the separate receipt suite.
